Subject: Shared gateway onramp: recommendation between Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

Charlotte / NetOps team —

Quick sync on the networking onramp for the Private deployment we're scoping for Finify. We sketched three candidate patterns and I attached a short decision matrix and a sketch (network-decision-matrix.xlsx, sketch-shared-gateway.png). High level question: which onramp pattern best balances your allowlist requirements, throughput expectations, and operational comfort?

Options we outlined: VPC Peering (account-to-account), AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoints), Site-to-Site VPN (customer-managed or managed VPN). We also described a hybrid 'shared gateway' pattern in the notes where control plane traffic uses PrivateLink and the data plane uses S2S or Direct Connect — that sketch is the second page.

Can you confirm the non-negotiables on your side:
- Do you need a stable static egress IP for allowlisting (yes/no)?
- Any maximum latency SLA for inference requests (p50/p99)?
- Ops preference: do you want us to run the VPN endpoint or will you manage the tunnel?

If you can reply with those skinny constraints I’ll pull together a recommended onramp and a short runbook. If easier, happy to do a 30-min call — suggested windows below.

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Subject: Re: Shared gateway onramp: recommendation between Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

Thanks Sean — quick answers from Finify ops:

- Static egress IP: Yes, we need a small set of stable IPs for our firewall allowlist (we cannot rely on ephemeral ENI IPs for the control plane).
- Latency SLA: For inference calls we target p50 < 60ms and p99 < 250ms from our east-us app region to the inference endpoint.
- VPN management: Our preference is that Redwood terminates one side of the VPN (managed by you) and we manage the other; we do have an option for a Direct Connect but not in the short-term.

A couple of notes on constraints:
- PCI-like control: customer data must never transit public internet egress on Redwood-managed paths (we need encryption in flight and clear routing controls).
- Audit/logging: we need flow logs / connection records shipped to our SIEM for the first 90 days of production.

From our POV PrivateLink looks attractive because it avoids cross-account route table complexity and is easy to allowlist; however we worry about cost and the static IP requirement — Public-facing PrivateLink endpoints still create ENIs per AZ.

If you can draft a recommended pattern that meets the above and the short runbook for firewall/DNS changes that would be great.

—Charlotte

Subject: RE: Shared gateway onramp: recommendation between Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

Adding our engineering read on tradeoffs — my notes below. I pulled numbers into the attached spreadsheet (tab: cost-latency-est).

Summary recommendation (engineer-first): recommend the "Shared Gateway" hybrid approach for Finify:
  - Control plane (API management, onboarding, health checks): AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint) bound to a Redwood-owned service network inside our customer VPC.
  - Data plane (inference request traffic and responses): Site-to-Site VPN (managed by Redwood) terminating into a dedicated customer-facing gateway VPC that forwards into the inference VPC with strict route policies and egress NAT to a fixed set of static IPs (NAT egress by Redwood).

Why this pattern:
- Static egress IPs: NAT + dedicated gateway VPC gives us stable outbound IPs for your firewall allowlist (satisfies Finify non-negotiable).
- Security & segmentation: PrivateLink for control plane keeps management traffic off public IPs and out of cross-account route table exposure; S2S makes customer data plane routing explicit and auditable.
- Latency: baseline numbers (rough): PrivateLink control traffic ~5–15ms within same region; S2S VPN (managed, good IKE parameters, single-AZ throughput) typical added latency ~10–40ms. In our perf tests with 99th percentile tuning we can expect p50 ~45ms, p99 ~180–220ms in an east-us to east-us pair. (These were measured on mTLS + small payloads — we’ll validate with a short perf run).
- Cost: PrivateLink has per-AZ ENI costs + hours; S2S managed tunnels have modest hourly charges and NAT gateway egress costs. Our spreadsheet shows PrivateLink-only for everything is higher OPEX (per-ENI) for multi-AZ deployments. Hybrid keeps per-request unit cost lower while meeting security.

Operational considerations / checklist:
- We will need three static egress IPs per region (for HA) — we propose to reserve and advertise those from the gateway VPC NAT (will provide exact IPs during onboarding).
- Route management: we will avoid peering because peering requires route-table updates across accounts and is brittle for multi-tenant scaling; peering also complicates egress path control.
- Monitoring: enable VPC Flow Logs on the gateway VPC and forward to Finify’s SIEM (we can push via AWS Kinesis/Firehose or customer-managed collector).
- Fallback plan: if VPN throughput is insufficient we have an escalation path to open a Direct Connect order (longer lead time) or provision extra VPN tunnels and use ECMP style routing.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Quick perf handshake: we (Redwood infra) spin up a short-lived test VPN tunnel and run a 2-hour perf profile with your app latency samples. (2 days)
2) Security run: share PrivateLink service principal, and our managed NAT IPs so you can validate firewall allowlists. (1–2 days)
3) Onboarding runbook: finish playbook (DNS, certs, x509 vs. mTLS options, flow logs). (3–4 days)

I can draft a one-page runbook and a sample Terraform snippet for the gateway NAT setup if that helps.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
